name: css-card-stacking

frames.best_why: Frame 6 shows two cards stacked, the green one peeking out behind the pink one, making the effect obvious.

tagline: Cards pin in place and slide over one another as you scroll.
summary: A full-screen section where tilted coloured cards stay pinned to the viewport and pile up on top of each other while the page scrolls, with a fixed heading beside them.
appearance: A dark navy page with a faint grid. Large rounded cards in green, pink, orange and blue sit tilted a few degrees, each holding a bold title, a short paragraph and a small black button. A fixed heading sits to the right of the stack.
behaviour: On scroll each card holds its place while the next rises and covers it, so earlier cards remain as a thin top edge. The side heading stays put throughout; scrolling back peels the cards away in reverse.
demo_content: Cards titled Image MouseTrail, Progressive Carousel, Responsive Drawer and Animated Globe with lorem-ipsum paragraphs.
search_phrases: sticky sections piling over each other
full screen cards that stay pinned
pile up effect for page sections
coloured cards sliding over each other
use_when: Several feature cards should be read one after another without losing the reader's place on the page.
avoid_when: Each card needs a full screen height, so a short page or a busy dashboard wastes vertical space.
customise: Card titles, copy, colours and links are written into the markup for each card; add or remove stacking blocks to change the pile. Scroll easing comes from the smooth-scroll wrapper.
weight_why: Pure CSS sticky cards plus a smooth-scroll wrapper; little work happens per frame.

a11y.note: Smooth scrolling ignores prefers-reduced-motion, and the view buttons have no visible focus style.

issues: Frames 1 and 2 show only the heading, so the stacking effect appears late in the clip.
polish_why: Clean layout and readable cards; the bright flat blocks and filler copy keep it ordinary.
